You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To obtain book name, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Recall the vague plot details (10 minutes)
Step 2. Search library database by keywords (15 minutes)
Step 3. Message a former literature professor (1 hour)
Step 4. Scroll through Goodreads "obscure books" lists (2 hours)
Step 5. Confirm the title with a book collector (30 minutes)
Step 6. Check a specialized bibliography (45 minutes)
Step 7. Browse an online forum for rare books (1 hour)
Step 8. Visit a local independent bookstore (1 hour)
Step 9. Post a description on a "tip of my tongue" subreddit (20 minutes)
Step 10. Look through old reading journals (30 minutes)
Step 11. Verify the ISBN on a publisher's site (10 minutes)
Step 12. Cross-reference the author's other works (40 minutes)
Step 13. Search digital archives for cover art (1 hour)
Step 14. Locate an old library card receipt (15 minutes)
Step 15. Read through forum replies (30 minutes)
Step 16. Ask a childhood friend if they remember the story (2 hours)
Step 17. Organize the known fragments of the story (30 minutes)
Step 18. Scan a digital copy of a similar book (2 hours)
Step 19. Check the "Books mentioned in" section of a wiki (20 minutes)
Step 20. Look for the book in a physical storage unit (3 hours)
Step 21. Find the box containing old school supplies (1 hour)
Step 22. Draft a list of possible character names (20 minutes)
Step 23. Email a specialist in the genre (15 minutes)
Step 24. Search through old emails for mentions of books (45 minutes)
Step 25. Consult a librarian via live chat (20 minutes)
Step 26. Review a list of award winners from that decade (1 hour)
Step 27. Create an account on a book identification site (5 minutes)
Step 28. Search for the illustrator’s portfolio (30 minutes)
Step 29. Examine a photograph of an old bookshelf (15 minutes)
Step 30. Check the local university's catalog (25 minutes)
Step 31. Post a query in a Facebook group for readers (10 minutes)
Step 32. Dig through a box of old magazines (2 hours)
Step 33. Search for the book’s description in French (45 minutes)
Step 34. Look at the "customers also bought" section on Amazon (15 minutes)
Step 35. Search for the publisher's defunct imprint (50 minutes)
Step 36. Look through a catalog of 1990s paperbacks (1 hour)
Step 37. Search for the book's setting on a map (10 minutes)
Step 38. Verify the publication year in an encyclopedia (20 minutes)
Step 39. Write down everything remembered about the ending (15 minutes)
Step 40. Read a blog post about lost media (1 hour)
Step 41. Contact a podcast that identifies lost books (30 minutes)
Step 42. Narrow down the search to a specific publisher (20 minutes)
Step 43. Order a copy of a potential match (5 minutes)
Step 44. Start a brainstorming session (30 minutes)
Step 45. Search for a specific quote from the book (1 hour)
Step 46. Look through a vintage book fair program (40 minutes)
Step 47. Check a list of books from a specific school curriculum (30 minutes)
Step 48. Ask a group of collectors on Discord (15 minutes)
Step 49. Check an online database of book blurbs (25 minutes)
Step 50. Finalize the book name (5 minutes)
